items.title: An equilibrium whose linearisation has all eigenvalues in the open left half-plane is locally exponentially stable
items.design_state: completed-local-argument; recorded in the batch notes
items.statement:
Let $n\ge1$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open with $0\in U$, and let $F:U\to\mathbb R^n$ be of class $C^1$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]) with $F(0)=0$. Put $A:=DF(0)$ ([[def-total-derivative-in-euclidean-space]], [[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]]) and suppose that every complex eigenvalue of $A$ ([[def-eigenvalue-eigenvector-eigenspace-and-spectrum]]) has negative real part.

Then $0$ is a locally exponentially stable equilibrium of $z'=F(z)$ ([[def-cm-equilibrium-and-lyapunov-stability]]): there are real numbers $\delta>0$, $\beta\ge1$ and $\gamma>0$ such that every maximal solution $z$ of $z'=F(z)$ with $\|z(0)\|_2<\delta$ is defined for all $t\ge0$ and satisfies

$$\|z(t)\|_2\le\beta e^{-\gamma t}\|z(0)\|_2\qquad(t\ge0).$$

In particular $0$ is Lyapunov stable and asymptotically stable in the sense of [[def-cm-equilibrium-and-lyapunov-stability]].
items.strategy: Build the positive definite Lyapunov matrix Q from the integral of e^{tA^T}e^{tA}, verify A^TQ+QA=-I by differentiating the integrand, and show that V=z^TQz decreases exponentially on a small compact sublevel set that traps every nearby solution by compact continuation.

references.title: F. Ramponi, Notes on Lyapunov's theorem, Sections 2-4: the Lyapunov function V = x^T P x with P = integral of e^{A^T t} Q e^{A t}, and stability via linearisation

G. Teschl, Ordinary Differential Equations and Dynamical Systems (AMS Graduate Studies in Mathematics 140, online edition), Section 6.6 (Liapunov's method) and Section 9.1, Theorem 9.1, printed pages 205-209 and 253-254

items.title: A hyperbolic equilibrium whose linearisation has an eigenvalue with positive real part is unstable
items.design_state: completed-local-argument; recorded in the batch notes
items.statement:
Let $n\ge1$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open with $0\in U$, and let $F:U\to\mathbb R^n$ be of class $C^1$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]) with $F(0)=0$. Put $A:=DF(0)$ ([[def-total-derivative-in-euclidean-space]], [[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]]) and suppose that

- no complex eigenvalue of $A$ ([[def-eigenvalue-eigenvector-eigenspace-and-spectrum]]) has real part $0$, and
- at least one eigenvalue of $A$ has positive real part.

Then the equilibrium $0$ is not Lyapunov stable ([[def-cm-equilibrium-and-lyapunov-stability]]): there is a real number $\varepsilon_0>0$ such that for every $\delta>0$ there exist $z_0\in U$ with $\|z_0\|_2<\delta$ and a time $t_1>0$ such that the maximal solution $z$ of $z'=F(z)$, $z(0)=z_0$ is defined on $[0,t_1]$ and satisfies

$$\|z(t_1)\|_2=\varepsilon_0 .$$
items.strategy: Use the indefinite form built from the unstable and stable Lyapunov matrices; it grows exponentially on a small ball along unstable data, and compact continuation forces arbitrarily small data to leave a fixed neighbourhood in finite time.

references.title: F. Ramponi, Notes on Lyapunov's theorem, Section 4 (instability when the linearisation has an eigenvalue with positive real part) and the counterexamples x' = -x^2, x' = x^2

G. Teschl, Ordinary Differential Equations and Dynamical Systems (AMS Graduate Studies in Mathematics 140, online edition), Section 9.2 (stable and unstable manifolds of a hyperbolic fixed point), printed pages 255-262

items.title: A strict local minimum of the potential gives a Lyapunov stable equilibrium of the mechanical system, by energy conservation
items.design_state: completed-local-argument; recorded in the batch notes
items.statement:
Let $n\ge1$, let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, let $M:\Omega\to M_n(\mathbb R)$ be a $C^2$ field of symmetric positive definite matrices, let $U:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ be $C^2$, let $q_0\in\Omega$ with $\nabla U(q_0)=0$, and suppose $q_0$ is a **strict local minimum** of $U$: there is $r_0>0$ with $\overline B(q_0,r_0)\subseteq\Omega$ and

$$U(q)>U(q_0)\qquad(0<\|q-q_0\|_2<r_0).$$

Let $G$ be the mechanical vector field of [[def-cm-mechanical-vector-field-and-energy-in-a-chart]] on $\Omega\times\mathbb R^n$, with energy $E(q,v)=\tfrac12v^{\mathsf T}M(q)v+U(q)$. Then $(q_0,0)$ is a Lyapunov stable equilibrium of $(q',v')=G(q,v)$ in the sense of [[def-cm-equilibrium-and-lyapunov-stability]]: for every $\varepsilon>0$ with $\overline B((q_0,0),\varepsilon)\subseteq\Omega\times\mathbb R^n$ there is $\delta>0$ such that every maximal solution $(q,v)$ with $\|(q(0),v(0))-(q_0,0)\|_2<\delta$ is defined for all $t\ge0$ and satisfies

$$\|(q(t),v(t))-(q_0,0)\|_2<\varepsilon\qquad(t\ge0).$$

No asymptotic stability is asserted.
items.strategy: Use exact energy conservation: E-E_0 has a positive minimum on the sphere of radius epsilon, continuity of E gives a delta, and the energy barrier forbids a first exit; compact continuation then gives forward existence for all time.

references.title: G. Teschl, Ordinary Differential Equations and Dynamical Systems (AMS Graduate Studies in Mathematics 140, online edition), Section 6.7, Theorem 6.16: a fixed point of Newton's equation is stable if the potential has a local minimum there
D. Tong, Classical Dynamics (Cambridge lecture notes, January 2015 version), Section 2.6 (stability of equilibria from the potential), printed pages 37-39

items.strategy: Exhibit the explicit blowing-up solution through every small positive initial value and refute the stability clause for every delta.

items.title: The amplitude of the sinusoidally forced damped oscillator: location and value of its maximum
items.statement:
Let $m>0$, $k>0$, $c>0$ and $f_0\ne0$. For $\Omega\ge0$ let

$$A(\Omega):=\frac{|f_0|}{\sqrt{(k-m\Omega^2)^2+c^2\Omega^2}}$$

be the amplitude about zero of the steady response of [[thm-cm-forced-oscillator-sinusoidal-response]] clause 1, and put

$$u_*:=\frac{k}{m}-\frac{c^2}{2m^2},\qquad \Omega_*:=\sqrt{u_*}\ \ \text{when }u_*>0 .$$

Then:

1. If $u_*>0$ (equivalently $c^2<2mk$), $A$ is strictly increasing on $[0,\Omega_*]$, strictly decreasing on $[\Omega_*,\infty)$, and its maximum on $[0,\infty)$ is attained at $\Omega_*$ and at no other point, with
$$A(\Omega_*)=\frac{2m|f_0|}{c\sqrt{4mk-c^2}} .$$
2. If $u_*\le0$ then $A$ is strictly decreasing on $[0,\infty)$ and its maximum on $[0,\infty)$ is attained at $\Omega=0$ and at no other point.
items.strategy: Write the denominator as an exact square m^2(u-u_*)^2+c^2(4mk-c^2)/(4m^2) in u=Omega^2, locate the vertex, and convert the monotonicity through the strictly decreasing maps x->1/x and x->sqrt(x).

references.title: K. Likharev, Essential Graduate Physics, Classical Mechanics (complete 252-page volume), Chapter 5 Section 5.1, Eqs. (5.18)-(5.22) and Fig. 5.1: the forced amplitude and the resonance peak, printed pages 4-5 of Chapter 5 (PDF pages 90-91)

I. Stewart, Advanced Classical Mechanics (MIT 8.09 Fall 2014, complete course text), Chapter 7 Section 7.1.3: 'the steady state forced motion (whose amplitude exhibits resonant behavior at omega_D = 1)', printed page 148

items.title: The harmonic (linear restoring) model: a declared linear force law with parameter $k>0$
items.statement:
**(i) Setting.** Work in the one-dimensional model class of
[[def-cm04-one-dimensional-models-and-equilibria]] with time window
$I_{0}=\mathbb R$, configuration domain $Q=\mathbb R$, a fixed mass $m>0$
and a **spring constant** $k>0$ of dimension $\mu\tau^{-2}$, read in newtons
per metre ([[def-cm01-units]]). The **harmonic model** is the model whose
force law is the **linear restoring force**
$$F(x,v):=-k\,x .$$
Its equation of motion is $m\,x''=-k\,x$, equivalently $m\,x''+k\,x=0$; the
model is autonomous and velocity-independent, and its potential is
$$U(x):=\tfrac12 k\,x^{2},$$
of dimension $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$ (joules), which presents the force law in
the sense of clause (d) of [[def-cm04-one-dimensional-models-and-equilibria]]:
$U$ is of class $C^{2}$ and $-U'(x)=-k\,x=F(x)$ ([[lem-derivative-of-a-power]],
[[def-derivative]]). The harmonic model is therefore a **conservative**
model of the class, with the potential representative $U$ declared above and
no residual force.

**(ii) Regularity and framework status.** The force law is affine in the
state; it is continuous, and $\lvert F(x)-F(x')\rvert=k\lvert x-x'\rvert\le
k\,\lVert(x,v)-(x',v')\rVert_{2}$, so it is locally Lipschitz in the state
variable with the global constant $k$, uniformly in time
([[def-locally-lipschitz-in-the-state-variable]]). The harmonic model is
thus an admissible model of the class of clause (a) of
[[def-cm04-one-dimensional-models-and-equilibria]], and the existence,
uniqueness and conservation statements of this page apply to it. It is
adopted as a restricted model class of the framework, at the same primitive
level as the force maps of [[post-cm02-force-superposition]]: the force law
is model input.

**(iii) Physical reading and regime.** The model idealizes a **restoring
force linear in the displacement**: an ideal spring, or the quadratic
approximation of a potential $U$ near a strict local minimum $x_{*}$ with $U''(x_*)>0$, where
the Taylor expansion of the effective potential begins with the quadratic
term $\tfrac12 U''(x_{*})(x-x_{*})^{2}$ and the linearized equation carries
the **effective spring constant** $U''(x_{*})$ (the sources' linearization
procedure). The model is adopted for a stated regime — displacements so
small that the neglected remainder of the potential is adequate for the
purpose at hand — and it is **not** claimed to describe large-amplitude
oscillations, nonlinear springs, plasticity, or any given real system. The
coefficient $k$ is a model parameter, not a constant of the framework; when
its value is taken from a calibration experiment, that value is an empirical
premise carrying the apparatus conditions and the measurement uncertainty,
and the framework asserts none of it here. The linear form is the simplest
restoring law satisfying the standing regularity; that is a modelling
convenience, not a derivation.

**(iv) Status.** Adopted assumption of the framework when a model invokes
it; it selects no law of nature on its own. Every consequence below is a
conditional statement about the declared equation of motion.
items.strategy: Adoption of the harmonic model: the linear restoring force -kx with declared spring constant k>0 and potential kx^2/2, with its regularity check, its reading as the quadratic approximation at a strict minimum of a potential, its regime of validity, and the status of k as model data.
items.physical_scope: Adoption of the harmonic oscillator as a restricted one-dimensional model: configuration domain the whole line, fixed mass m>0, force law F(x)=-k x with declared spring constant k>0 of dimension mass per time squared, and potential U(x)=k x^2/2. The model is a linear idealization of a restoring force, adopted for a stated regime (small displacements from a stable equilibrium, in which the quadratic term of the potential is the adequate approximation, as in the sources' linearization procedure); the spring constant is model data whose value, if taken from measurement, is an empirical premise with its own conditions and uncertainty. The item asserts no value of k, no claim that the model applies to a given spring or oscillation, and no measured result.

items.title: Existence, uniqueness and conservation of energy for a one-dimensional conservative model: phase curves lie in energy level sets and the velocity is determined by the position
items.statement:
Adopt a **conservative one-dimensional model**: the class of clause (a) of
[[def-cm04-one-dimensional-models-and-equilibria]] with a **time- and
velocity-independent** force law presented through a potential, that is
$$F(x)=-U'(x)\qquad(x\in Q)$$
for a function $U:Q\to\mathbb R$ of class $C^{2}$ (so the residual force of
clause (d) of that definition vanishes identically and the model is a global
potential model). Write
$$E(x,v)=\tfrac12 m v^{2}+U(x)$$
for the energy function of [[def-cm04-phase-plane-and-energy-level-sets]]
clause (b). Then:

1. **Existence and uniqueness.** Every datum $(t_{0},x_{0},v_{0})$ with
   $t_{0}\in I_{0}$, $x_{0}\in Q$, $v_{0}\in\mathbb R$ has exactly one
   **maximal motion**: a motion $x:J_{\max}\to Q$ with $x(t_{0})=x_{0}$ and
   $x'(t_{0})=v_{0}$ that has no extension to a motion on a strictly larger
   interval. Its interval $J_{\max}$ is open, contains $t_{0}$ and is
   contained in $I_{0}$, and every motion of the model with the same datum is
   the restriction of $x$ to a subinterval.
2. **Energy conservation.** For every motion $x:J\to Q$ the function
   $t\mapsto E(x(t),x'(t))$ is constant on $J$.
3. **Level-set containment and velocity determination.** Let $x:J\to Q$ be
   a motion with datum $(t_{0},x_{0},v_{0})$ and let $E_{0}:=E(x_{0},v_{0})$.
   Then $U(x(t))\le E_{0}$ for every $t\in J$; if $U(x(t))<E_{0}$ then
   $$x'(t)=\pm\sqrt{\frac{2\bigl(E_{0}-U(x(t))\bigr)}{m}},$$
   the two signs giving the only two possible values; and $x'(t)=0$ holds
   exactly when $U(x(t))=E_{0}$. In particular the phase curve of $x$ is
   contained in the energy level set $\Sigma_{E_{0}}$ of clause (b) of
   [[def-cm04-phase-plane-and-energy-level-sets]].
4. **Rest motions.** A point $x_{*}\in Q$ is an equilibrium of the model if
   and only if $U'(x_{*})=0$; in that case the constant curve
   $x\equiv x_{*}$ is the maximal motion with datum $(t_{0},x_{*},0)$, and
   conversely the maximal motion with datum $(t_{0},x_{*},0)$ is constant
   exactly when $U'(x_{*})=0$.

The statement is conditional on the declared potential $U$: replacing $U$ by
$U+c$ with a constant $c$ changes $E$ on the whole phase plane by $c$ and
leaves clauses 1, 3 and 4 unchanged. No claim of periodicity, boundedness of
the position or of the velocity, or approach to an equilibrium is made.
items.strategy: A conditional deduction: apply the maximal-solution theorem to the phase system for existence and uniqueness, differentiate the energy along a motion using the equation of motion to obtain conservation, and read off the level-set containment, the velocity determination and the correspondence between rest points and equilibria.
items.physical_scope: The basic dynamical content of a conservative one-dimensional model: every datum has exactly one maximal motion; the mechanical energy k x-dot^2/2 + U(x) (written m x-dot^2/2 + U(x)) is constant along every motion; a motion of initial energy E_0 keeps its position in the sublevel set {U <= E_0}, and where U is strictly below E_0 its velocity is one of the two square-root values determined by the position; every non-turning phase point of the motion lies on the energy level set of E_0; and the constant motions are exactly the rest motions at equilibria. The result is a conditional deduction from the declared potential presentation; it asserts no periodicity, no boundedness of the motion, no asymptotic behaviour and no measured value.

items.title: A strict local minimum of the potential is a Lyapunov stable equilibrium of the conservative one-dimensional model, and its linearisation is an oscillator-type model
items.statement:
Adopt a conservative one-dimensional model as in
[[pthm-cm04-conservative-motion-and-energy]]: the class of
[[def-cm04-one-dimensional-models-and-equilibria]] with force law
$F(x)=-U'(x)$ for a potential $U:Q\to\mathbb R$ of class $C^{2}$, phase
system $G_{F}(x,v)=(v,-U'(x)/m)$ on $Q\times\mathbb R$, and energy
$E=\tfrac12mv^{2}+U$. Let $x_{*}\in Q$ be a **strict local minimum** of $U$:
there is $r_{0}>0$ with $\overline B(x_{*},r_{0})\subseteq Q$ and
$U(x)>U(x_{*})$ for $0<\lvert x-x_{*}\rvert<r_{0}$. Then:

1. **Lyapunov stability.** $(x_{*},0)$ is a Lyapunov stable rest point of
   the phase system in the sense of [[def-cm-equilibrium-and-lyapunov-stability]]:
   for every $\varepsilon>0$ with $\overline B((x_{*},0),\varepsilon)\subseteq
   Q\times\mathbb R$ there is $\delta>0$ such that the unique maximal solution of the autonomous phase equation through the datum of every motion $x$ of the
   model with $\lVert(x(t_{0}),x'(t_{0}))-(x_{*},0)\rVert_{2}<\delta$ for some
   $t_{0}\in I_{0}$ is defined for all $t\ge t_{0}$ and satisfies
   $$\bigl\lVert\bigl(x(t)-x_{*},\,x'(t)\bigr)\bigr\rVert_{2}<\varepsilon \qquad(t\ge t_{0}).$$
   Here $x$ in the displayed all-time bound denotes that maximal extension; on the original motion interval it agrees with the given motion. The autonomous equation is read on $\mathbb R\times Q\times\mathbb R$, even when the declared time window $I_0$ is smaller; no enlargement of that declared window is asserted. The norm is the Euclidean norm on $\mathbb R^{2}$ of
   [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]; the balls are those of
   [[def-metric-ball]]. No asymptotic stability and no attraction are
   asserted.

2. **Linearisation.** $U''(x_{*})$ exists ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]),
   the phase field $G_{F}$ is totally differentiable at $(x_{*},0)$ with
   $$DG_{F}(x_{*},0)(\delta x,\delta v)=\Bigl(\delta v,\ -\frac{U''(x_{*})}{m}\,\delta x\Bigr),$$
   and the linearised equation is
   $$m\,\xi''+U''(x_{*})\,\xi=0,$$
   which is the equation of the oscillator-type model of clause (f) of
   [[def-cm04-one-dimensional-models-and-equilibria]] with data
   $(m,0,U''(x_{*}),0)$ ([[def-cm-oscillator-model-and-phase-system]]). If in
   addition $U''(x_{*})>0$, then that linearised model is the harmonic model
   of [[post-cm04-harmonic-model]] with spring constant $U''(x_{*})$, and its
   undamped frequency in the sense of
   [[def-cm-oscillator-model-and-phase-system]] is $\sqrt{U''(x_{*})/m}$.

The statement is conditional on the potential $U$ and on the strict local
minimum; no conclusion is drawn for a critical point that is only a weak
minimum, a maximum, or a point where $U''$ vanishes identically on one side.
items.strategy: A conditional deduction: identify the scalar phase system with the one-dimensional constant-metric instance of the mathematical mechanical system, apply the energy-stability theorem at the strict minimum, and read the linearisation and its frequency from the linearisation proposition.
items.physical_scope: The equilibrium theory of a conservative one-dimensional model near a strict local minimum of its potential: the rest point is Lyapunov stable, with the Euclidean phase-plane norm, and its linearisation is the oscillator-type model with data (m,0,U''(x_*),0), which is the harmonic model with spring constant U''(x_*) when that number is positive. The statement is conditional on the declared potential and its strict local minimum; it asserts no asymptotic stability, no attraction and no instability in any case, and no measured value.

items.title: The motions of the harmonic model are the sinusoids $A\cos(\omega(t-t_0))+B\sin(\omega(t-t_0))$: amplitude and phase, the least period, the conserved energy $kR^2/2$ and the elliptical phase curves
items.statement:
Adopt the harmonic model of [[post-cm04-harmonic-model]]: the
one-dimensional model of [[def-cm04-one-dimensional-models-and-equilibria]]
with $m>0$, $k>0$, force law $F(x)=-kx$ and potential $U(x)=\tfrac12kx^{2}$.
Write
$$\omega:=\sqrt{\frac{k}{m}}>0$$
for its **undamped frequency** in the sense of
[[def-cm-oscillator-model-and-phase-system]]. Then:

1. **Motions.** Let $J\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval with nonempty
   interior and let $t_{0}\in J$. A curve $x:J\to\mathbb R$ is a motion of the
   model on $J$ if and only if there are reals $A,B$ with
   $$x(t)=A\cos\bigl(\omega(t-t_{0})\bigr)+B\sin\bigl(\omega(t-t_{0})\bigr) \qquad(t\in J).$$
   For every datum $(t_{0},x_{0},v_{0})$ there is exactly one maximal motion,
   it is defined on all of $\mathbb R$, and its coefficients are
   $A=x_{0}$, $B=v_{0}/\omega$; every motion with that datum is its
   restriction.
All claims involving every real time, periods or the whole phase ellipse below refer to the unique maximal extension of clause 1; on a local motion interval the same formulas hold by restriction.

2. **Amplitude and phase.** With $A,B$ as in clause 1 put
   $R:=\sqrt{A^{2}+B^{2}}$. Then $\lvert x(t)\rvert\le R$ for every $t$; if
   $R>0$ there is a real $\varphi$ with $\cos\varphi=A/R$ and
   $\sin\varphi=B/R$, and then
   $$x(t)=R\cos\bigl(\omega(t-t_{0})-\varphi\bigr)\qquad(t\in\mathbb R).$$
   If $R=0$ the motion is the rest motion $x\equiv0$.
3. **Period and frequency.** For every motion $x(t+T)=x(t)$ holds for all
   $t$ whenever $\omega T\in2\pi\mathbb Z$. If $R>0$, conversely every
   period $T>0$ of $x$ satisfies $\omega T\in2\pi\mathbb Z$, so the **least
   positive period** of the motion is $T_{\mathrm{per}}=2\pi/\omega$, and the
   **frequency** in cycles per second is $f=1/T_{\mathrm{per}}=\omega/(2\pi)$.
   If $R=0$ every $T$ is a period.
4. **Energy and phase curves.** Along every motion with coefficients $A,B$
   the mechanical energy is
   $$E\bigl(x(t),x'(t)\bigr)=\tfrac12k\bigl(A^{2}+B^{2}\bigr)=\tfrac12kR^{2}$$
   for every $t$, the phase curve is contained in the ellipse
   $$\Sigma_{R}:=\Bigl\{(x,v)\in\mathbb R^{2}:\frac{x^{2}}{R^{2}}+\frac{v^{2}}{\omega^{2}R^{2}}=1\Bigr\}$$
   when $R>0$, and it is exactly that ellipse: every point of $\Sigma_{R}$
   lies on the phase curve of the motion and is attained at exactly the times
   $t=t_{0}+\bigl(\theta_{1}+\varphi+2\pi n\bigr)/\omega$, $n\in\mathbb Z$,
   for the appropriate $\theta_{1}$. For $R=0$ the phase curve is the single
   point $(0,0)$, which is also the level set of energy $0$.
5. **Rest point.** The origin $(0,0)$ is the only rest point of the model,
   and it is Lyapunov stable, by
   [[pthm-cm04-equilibrium-stability-at-a-strict-minimum]]; no asymptotic
   stability is asserted.

The statement uses the declared data $m,k$ only through $\omega$ and the
energy; no value of $m$ or $k$ is asserted, and no real oscillator is claimed
to obey the model.
items.strategy: A direct deduction: transport the mathematical classification of the homogeneous oscillator to an arbitrary base time, prove the unit-circle parametrisation used for the phase form and the ellipse coverage, compute the energy along the explicit family, read the least period from the fundamental period of cosine, and apply the strict-minimum theorem at the origin.
items.physical_scope: The complete motion analysis of the harmonic model with m>0 and k>0: every motion is a sinusoid about any chosen base time, with the initial data as coefficients; the amplitude and phase form; the least period 2 pi/omega and the frequency in cycles per second; the conserved mechanical energy k R^2/2; the phase curve is exactly the ellipse of the energy level set, with the two semiaxes; and the origin is the unique rest point and is Lyapunov stable. The result is a conditional deduction from the adopted linear force law; it asserts no value of k or m, no application to a real spring, and no asymptotic stability.

items.title: Strictly damped oscillator: explicit decay bounds, convergence to rest and asymptotic stability of the origin
items.statement:
Adopt the damped oscillator model of [[post-cm04-linear-damping-model]] with
$m>0$, $k>0$ and $c>0$ (strict damping), force law $F(x,v)=-kx-cv$ and
energy $E(x,v)=\tfrac12mv^{2}+\tfrac12kx^{2}$. Write
$\Delta=c^{2}-4mk$, $\gamma=c/(2m)>0$,
$\lambda_{\pm}=(-c\pm\sqrt{\Delta})/(2m)$ for $\Delta\ge0$,
$\lambda=-c/(2m)$ for $\Delta=0$ and $\omega=\sqrt{4mk-c^{2}}/(2m)$ for
$\Delta<0$. Then:

1. **Motion bounds.** For every motion $x:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ of the model
   with datum $(0,x_{0},v_{0})$ and $r_{0}:=\sqrt{x_{0}^{2}+v_{0}^{2}}$ the
   following bounds hold for all $t\ge0$, with the coefficients $A,B$ of the
   classification of [[pthm-cm04-damped-motion]]:
   - $\Delta>0$: $\lvert x(t)\rvert\le(\lvert A\rvert+\lvert
     B\rvert)e^{\lambda_{+}t}$ and
     $\lvert x'(t)\rvert\le\bigl(\lvert\lambda_{+}\rvert\lvert
     A\rvert+\lvert\lambda_{-}\rvert\lvert B\rvert\bigr)e^{\lambda_{+}t}$;
   - $\Delta=0$: $\lvert x(t)\rvert\le(\lvert A\rvert+\lvert
     B\rvert t)e^{\lambda t}$ and
     $\lvert x'(t)\rvert\le\bigl(\lvert\lambda A+B\rvert+\lvert\lambda
     B\rvert t\bigr)e^{\lambda t}$;
   - $\Delta<0$: $\lvert x(t)\rvert\le(\lvert A\rvert+\lvert
     B\rvert)e^{-\gamma t}$ and $\lvert x'(t)\rvert\le\bigl(\lvert\omega
     B-\gamma A\rvert+\lvert\gamma B+\omega A\rvert\bigr)e^{-\gamma t}$;
   and there are constants $C_{1},C_{2}>0$, depending only on $(m,k,c)$, with
   $$\lvert x(t)\rvert\le C_{1}r_{0},\qquad\lvert x'(t)\rvert\le C_{2}r_{0} \qquad(t\ge0).$$
2. **Convergence.** For every maximal motion, $x(t)\to0$ and $x'(t)\to0$ as
   $t\to+\infty$ ([[def-limits-at-infinity]]).
3. **Asymptotic stability.** The rest point $(0,0)$ is Lyapunov stable and
   globally asymptotically stable in the sense of
   [[def-cm-equilibrium-and-lyapunov-stability]] for the model's phase
   system: for every $\varepsilon>0$ there is $\delta>0$ such that every
   maximal motion with $\lVert(x(t_{0}),x'(t_{0}))\rVert_{2}<\delta$ for some
   $t_{0}$ is defined for all $t\ge t_{0}$ and satisfies
   $\lVert(x(t),x'(t))\rVert_{2}<\varepsilon$ for all $t\ge t_{0}$; and
   every maximal motion satisfies $\lVert(x(t),x'(t))\rVert_{2}\to0$ as
   $t\to+\infty$. The norm is the Euclidean norm on $\mathbb R^{2}$
   ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]]).

The constants are explicit in the proof and no value of $m,k,c$ is asserted.
items.strategy: A case deduction: bound the coefficients of the three solution families by the initial phase norm, derive the explicit decay bounds from the position estimates and the energy monotonicity, obtain convergence of position and velocity, and assemble the uniform bound that yields Lyapunov stability and the global attraction of the rest point.
items.physical_scope: The strictly damped oscillator with m>0, k>0, c>0: every motion is bounded by explicit constants times the initial phase norm, tends to zero together with its velocity, and the origin of the phase plane is a globally asymptotically stable rest point in the sense of the framework's stability definition. The result is a conditional deduction from the declared model data; it asserts no value of the parameters, no measured decay rate and no behaviour of any real damper, and its constants are the explicit ones produced by the classification.

items.title: The driven oscillator: the sinusoidal steady response, its amplitude and maximum, bounded motions for $c>0$ and at $c=0$ off resonance, and the unbounded resonant motions at $c=0$
items.statement:
Adopt the sinusoidally driven oscillator model of
[[post-cm04-sinusoidal-drive-model]] with data $m>0$, $k>0$, $c\ge0$,
$f_{0}\in\mathbb R$ and $\Omega>0$, force law
$F(t,x,v)=f_{0}\cos(\Omega t)-kx-cv$ and equation
$m\,x''+cx'+kx=f_{0}\cos(\Omega t)$. Put
$$\omega_{0}:=\sqrt{\frac{k}{m}},\qquad D:=k-m\Omega^{2}+i\,c\,\Omega\in\mathbb C,$$
and define the **steady response**
$$x_{p}(t):=\operatorname{Re}\Bigl(\frac{f_{0}e^{i\Omega t}}{D}\Bigr) =\frac{f_{0}\bigl[(k-m\Omega^{2})\cos(\Omega t)+c\,\Omega\sin(\Omega t)\bigr]} {(k-m\Omega^{2})^{2}+c^{2}\Omega^{2}}\qquad(D\neq0),$$
with **amplitude** $A(\Omega):=\lvert f_{0}\rvert/\sqrt{(k-m\Omega^{2})^{2}+c^{2}\Omega^{2}}$,
and in the exceptional case $c=0$, $\Omega=\omega_{0}$ define
$x_{p}(t):=f_{0}t\sin(\omega_{0}t)/(2m\omega_{0})$. All all-time boundedness, convergence and unboundedness claims below refer to maximal motions on $\mathbb R$; local motions are their restrictions as in clause 2. Then:

1. **Steady response.** If $D\neq0$ — that is $c>0$, or $c=0$ and
   $\Omega\neq\omega_{0}$ — then $x_{p}$ is a motion of the model on
   $\mathbb R$, of period $2\pi/\Omega$, with amplitude $A(\Omega)$ in the
   sense $\lvert x_{p}(t)\rvert\le A(\Omega)$ for all $t$ and equality at
   suitable times.
2. **Reduction to the homogeneous model.** Every datum has exactly one
   maximal motion, it is defined on all of $\mathbb R$, and every motion
   $x$ of the model on an interval with nonempty interior can be written
   $x=x_{p}+y$, where $x_{p}$ is the particular motion of clause 1, or the
   resonant motion in the exceptional case, and $y$ is a motion of the damped
   homogeneous model with the same $m$, $c$, $k$ (and is a harmonic motion
   of [[post-cm04-harmonic-model]] when $c=0$).
3. **Strictly damped case $c>0$.** For every $\Omega>0$ the following hold:
   every motion is bounded on $[0,\infty)$; and
   $x(t)-x_{p}(t)\to0$ and $x'(t)-x_{p}'(t)\to0$ as $t\to+\infty$. Moreover
   $x_{p}$ is the unique motion with datum
   $(t_{0},x_{p}(t_{0}),x_{p}'(t_{0}))$ for any $t_{0}\in\mathbb R$. The
   amplitude function $\Omega\mapsto A(\Omega)$ has the following shape when $f_0\ne0$: if
   $c^{2}<2mk$ it is strictly increasing on $(0,\Omega_{*})$ and strictly
   decreasing on $(\Omega_{*},\infty)$ with
   $$\Omega_{*}=\sqrt{\frac{k}{m}-\frac{c^{2}}{2m^{2}}},\qquad A(\Omega_{*})=\frac{2m\lvert f_{0}\rvert}{c\sqrt{4mk-c^{2}}};$$
   if $c^{2}\ge2mk$ it is strictly decreasing on $(0,\infty)$. For $f_0=0$ the amplitude is identically zero.
4. **Undamped case away from resonance.** For $c=0$ and
   $\Omega\neq\omega_{0}$ every motion is bounded on $\mathbb R$.
5. **Undamped resonance.** For $c=0$, $\Omega=\omega_{0}$ and $f_{0}\neq0$
   the motion $x_{p}(t)=f_{0}t\sin(\omega_{0}t)/(2m\omega_{0})$ is unbounded
   on $[0,\infty)$, and every motion of the model is unbounded on
   $[0,\infty)$, although the drive $t\mapsto f_{0}\cos(\omega_{0}t)$ is
   bounded.
6. **Off the singular cases.** For $c>0$ the denominator never vanishes and
   every $\Omega>0$ is admissible; for $c=0$ the exceptional frequency is
   exactly $\Omega=\omega_{0}$. Consequently the boundedness assertions of
   clauses 3 and 4 hold for $c>0$, and for $c=0$ away from $\Omega=\omega_{0}$,
   and also at undamped resonance when $f_0=0$; for a nonzero drive clause 5 gives unboundedness at undamped resonance.

The statement is read for the declared model data; no value of any parameter
and no measured response is asserted.
items.strategy: A case analysis: verify the complex steady response and its real form, reduce every motion to the particular motion plus a homogeneous motion by linearity, use the strictly damped decay for the boundedness and convergence clauses, use the harmonic boundedness for the undamped off-resonant case, exhibit the unbounded resonant motion at zero damping, and read the amplitude maximum from the amplitude proposition.
items.physical_scope: The response of the driven oscillator model with m>0, k>0, c>=0, drive amplitude f_0 and angular frequency Omega>0: the explicit steady sinusoidal response and its amplitude |f_0|/sqrt((k-m Omega^2)^2+c^2 Omega^2) whenever the denominator does not vanish; the reduction of every motion to the steady response plus a homogeneous motion; boundedness of every motion in the strictly damped case, with exponential convergence of the transient to the steady response; boundedness for c=0 away from Omega=sqrt(k/m); unbounded motions at c=0 and Omega=sqrt(k/m) with nonzero amplitude, so boundedness fails exactly in the off-singular-case sense; and the amplitude maximum of the steady response for c>0. The result is a conditional deduction from the declared drive and damping models; it asserts no measured resonance curve, no value of any parameter and no behaviour of an apparatus.

items.title: Scope and limits of the one-dimensional conservative and dissipative models: declared class, approximation status, empirical parameters and open extensions
items.statement:
Scope and limits

- **The one-dimensional class is declared, not derived.** The models of this
  page are restricted model classes of
  [[def-cm04-one-dimensional-models-and-equilibria]]: a scalar coordinate,
  a mass and a scalar force law with the standing regularity. Their relation
  to motions of the three-dimensional force branch along a straight line, or
  to effective one-dimensional reductions of constrained systems such as the
  pendulum, is a modelling identification that a consumer item states and
  uses explicitly; this page contains no three-dimensional reduction
  theorem, and the pendulum example of the companion page declares its
  effective model equation with its source support.

- **Declared assumptions versus deductions.** The harmonic, damped and driven
  models are adopted postulates
  ([[post-cm04-harmonic-model]], [[post-cm04-linear-damping-model]],
  [[post-cm04-sinusoidal-drive-model]]); everything else on the page is a
  conditional deduction from them: existence and uniqueness, energy
  conservation and level-set containment
  ([[pthm-cm04-conservative-motion-and-energy]]), Lyapunov stability at a
  strict minimum ([[pthm-cm04-equilibrium-stability-at-a-strict-minimum]]),
  the sinusoid classification, energy and phase ellipses
  ([[pthm-cm04-harmonic-motion]]), the damping classification and the
  dissipation identity ([[pthm-cm04-damped-motion]]), decay and asymptotic
  stability ([[pthm-cm04-damped-decay-and-stability]]), and the response,
  boundedness and resonance statements
  ([[pthm-cm04-resonance-and-boundedness]]). No deduction here establishes
  that a real system obeys a model.

- **The harmonic model is a local quadratic approximation.** Adopting
  $U(x)=\tfrac12kx^{2}$ reproduces the quadratic term of the potential near
  a strict minimum and the linearized equation about it; the approximation
  is exact only for the declared model. For the pendulum, the difference
  between the nonlinear and the linearized motion is bounded only in the
  finite-time sense of
  [[prop-cm-pendulum-small-angle-linearization-bound]], with the explicit
  small-amplitude and time hypotheses of that statement; no uniform-in-time
  approximation is asserted anywhere on this page.

- **The drag is phenomenological and fluctuation-free.** The linear drag
  model is adopted for a stated viscous regime; its coefficient depends on
  body and medium; the random component of the environment's force is
  neglected, a restriction the recorded source attaches to an energy-scale
  condition. No fluctuation–dissipation relation, no derivation of $c$ and
  no validity outside the linear regime is claimed; regimes of quadratic
  drag or of Coulomb friction are different models outside this page.

- **The drive is prescribed and sinusoidal.** The driven model's force is a
  function of time alone with an idealized sinusoidal waveform; no
  back-reaction of the motion on the drive, no non-sinusoidal waveform and
  no apparatus characterization is part of the model. The boundedness and
  resonance clauses of [[pthm-cm04-resonance-and-boundedness]] are
  statements about this model's motions.

- **Measured parameters are empirical premises.** The values of $m$, $k$,
  $c$, $f_{0}$ and $\Omega$ are model data; when a value is obtained from a
  calibration or an apparatus specification, its uncertainty, the
  calibration method and the operating conditions are premises of any
  comparison with observation, and agreement of a model prediction with
  data is statistical evidence about the combined model and apparatus
  assumptions, never a proof of the model. This page asserts no measured
  value and no empirical agreement.

- **Stability conclusions and their boundaries.** The conservative model has
  a Lyapunov stable rest point at a strict minimum; the strictly damped
  model has a globally asymptotically stable rest point; no conclusion is
  drawn at degenerate critical points, at maxima, or for the undamped driven
  model. In particular the linearized repulsive frequency of a maximum is
  not used to claim nonlinear instability of the model.

- **Open extensions.** Nonlinear oscillators with large amplitude (the exact
  pendulum and its secular drift), parametric resonance, nonlinear damping
  and self-oscillation, dissipative models with fluctuations, and numerical
  integration studies are outside this page's scope and belong to the later
  pages of the track; the recorded sources' treatments of those topics are
  not prerequisites of the claims proved here.
items.strategy: A scope remark: it separates declared model assumptions from conditional deductions and approximation or empirical interfaces on the page, records the finite-time character of the small-angle bound, the phenomenological and fluctuation-free character of the drag, the prescribed-drive idealisation, the status of measured parameters as empirical premises, the boundaries of the stability conclusions and the open extensions.

The remark asserts no new mathematical or physical claim and no measured value.

items.statement:
Declare the damped oscillator model of [[post-cm04-linear-damping-model]] with
$$m=1\ \mathrm{kg},\qquad k=1\ \mathrm{N/m},$$
and the common datum at $t_{0}=0$
$$x_{0}=1\ \mathrm{m},\qquad v_{0}=0\ \mathrm{m/s},$$
for each of the three drag coefficients
$$c=1,\quad c=2,\quad c=5\qquad(\mathrm{kg/s}).$$
The claims checked below are that the three displayed curves are the unique
maximal motions with this datum in the three cases, that all three have
initial energy $\tfrac12$ J and satisfy $E'(t)=-c\,x'(t)^{2}$, and that the
decay bounds of [[pthm-cm04-damped-decay-and-stability]] hold with the
displayed constants:

$$\begin{aligned} c=1:\quad & x(t)=e^{-t/2}\Bigl(\cos\frac{\sqrt3\,t}{2}+\frac{1}{\sqrt3}\sin\frac{\sqrt3\,t}{2}\Bigr),\\ c=2:\quad & x(t)=(1+t)e^{-t},\\ c=5:\quad & x(t)=\frac{5+\sqrt{21}}{2\sqrt{21}}\,e^{\frac{-5+\sqrt{21}}{2}t} +\frac{\sqrt{21}-5}{2\sqrt{21}}\,e^{\frac{-5-\sqrt{21}}{2}t}. \end{aligned}$$

items.title: The ideal pendulum as an effective one-dimensional model: strict minimum, stability, the small-angle harmonic model and the finite-time error bound with its numbers
items.statement:
Adopt the **ideal planar pendulum in the angle coordinate** as an effective scalar mechanical chart model. Its scalar equation has the form of the equations analyzed in [[def-cm04-one-dimensional-models-and-equilibria]], with
configuration domain $\mathbb R$, coordinate $\theta$ (the angle from the
downward vertical, in radians), effective mass parameter
$$m_{\mathrm{ef}}:=m\,l^{2}>0,\qquad\text{force law}\qquad F(\theta):=-m\,g\,l\,\sin\theta,$$
and constants $m,l,g>0$ of dimensions mass, length and length per time
squared ([[def-cm01-units]]). Its equation of motion is
$$m\,l^{2}\,\theta''=-m\,g\,l\,\sin\theta,\qquad\text{equivalently}\qquad \theta''=-\frac{g}{l}\sin\theta,$$
the recorded source's point-pendulum equation (Eq. (1.18) there) read as an effective one-dimensional system. Here the coordinate is a dimensionless angle, $m_{\mathrm{ef}}=ml^2$ is an effective kinetic coefficient of dimension $\mu\ell^2$, and $F$ is a generalized torque of dimension $\mu\ell^2\tau^{-2}$; it is not the literal length coordinate and mass-in-kilograms class of that definition. The stability and linearization calculations use its autonomous scalar equation as the constant-metric mathematical chart system with $M=m_{\mathrm{ef}}$. The claims checked below are:

1. the model is conservative with potential $U(\theta)=-mgl\cos\theta$, and
   $\theta=0$ is a strict local minimum of $U$;
2. the hanging rest point $(\theta,\theta')=(0,0)$ is Lyapunov stable, and
   the linearised model at it is the oscillator-type model with data
   $(m_{\mathrm{ef}},0,mgl,0)$, which is harmonic with spring constant $mgl$
   and frequency $\omega=\sqrt{g/l}$;
3. at $g=l=1$, radius $r=1/2$, amplitude $\delta=1/100$ and $T=1$, the
   difference between the exact motion and the harmonic motion with the same
   datum obeys
   $$\lVert z(t)-y(t)\rVert_{2}\le\frac{t\,e^{3t}}{12\cdot10^{4}}\qquad(0\le t\le1),\qquad\lVert z(1)-y(1)\rVert_{2}\le\frac{e^{3}}{12\cdot10^{4}} \approx1.67\cdot10^{-4},$$
   the source-supported bound of
   [[prop-cm-pendulum-small-angle-linearization-bound]];
4. the pendulum model is not harmonic: the harmonic energy
   $\tfrac12m_{\mathrm{ef}}\theta'^{2}+\tfrac12mgl\theta^{2}$ is not
   conserved along exact motions, with
   $$\frac{d}{dt}\Bigl[\tfrac12m_{\mathrm{ef}}\theta'^{2} +\tfrac12mgl\theta^{2}\Bigr]=mgl\,\theta'\,(\theta-\sin\theta),$$
   which is positive at the phase point $(\theta,\theta')=(\pi/2,1)$.
items.strategy: A worked check: verify the effective pendulum model's potential presentation and strict minimum, apply the stability and linearisation clauses, transport the source-supported finite-time small-angle bound with its explicit numbers at g=l=1, and exhibit the non-conservation of the harmonic energy along the exact motion.

The item asserts no measured value, no period formula for finite amplitudes and no derivation of the effective equation from the constrained system.

items.title: The coupled quadratic oscillator model: mass metric, stiffness, generalized force, modal vocabulary and the small-oscillation model at a mechanical equilibrium
items.statement:
**(a) Data of a coupled quadratic model.** A **coupled quadratic model** (a
**quadratic oscillator model**) is declared by the following data: an integer
$n\ge1$, the number of **degrees of freedom**; a **mass metric matrix**
$M\in M_{n}(\mathbb R)$, symmetric and positive definite, that is
$M=M^{\mathsf T}$ and $v^{\mathsf T}Mv>0$ for every nonzero
$v\in\mathbb R^{n}$ ([[def-matrix-product-and-identity-matrix]],
[[def-euclidean-inner-product]]); a **stiffness matrix**
$K\in M_{n}(\mathbb R)$, symmetric, $K=K^{\mathsf T}$; and, when the model is
read as forced, an interval $I_{0}\subseteq\mathbb R$ with nonempty interior
([[def-interval]]) together with a continuous **generalized force**
$J:I_{0}\to\mathbb R^{n}$ ([[def-vector-valued-functions-limits-and-continuity]]).
The coordinates $q_{1},\dots,q_{n}$ of $\mathbb R^{n}$ are read in the chart
in which the model is declared and carry declared dimensions
$\gamma_{1},\dots,\gamma_{n}$ and units, and time is read in seconds and mass
in kilograms ([[def-cm01-units]]). The data carry the dimensions

$$[M_{ij}]=\mu\ell^{2}\gamma_{i}^{-1}\gamma_{j}^{-1},\qquad [K_{ij}]=\mu\ell^{2}\gamma_{i}^{-1}\gamma_{j}^{-1}\tau^{-2},\qquad [J_{i}]=\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}\gamma_{i}^{-1},$$

so that $\tfrac12v^{\mathsf T}Mv$, $\tfrac12q^{\mathsf T}Kq$ and the pairing
$J\cdot\delta q$ of the generalized force with a coordinate variation all have
the energy dimension $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$; if the coordinate $q_{i}$ is
length-valued, $\gamma_{i}=\ell$, the entry $J_{i}$ has the force dimension
$\mu\ell\tau^{-2}$. This is the dimension bookkeeping of a generalized
coordinate description in the sense of
[[def-cm07-generalized-coordinates-and-forces]], whose kinetic metric and
generalized forces are the framework objects the data present; the matrices
$M$ and $K$ are model parameters, not measured quantities.

**(b) Model equation, motions and phase system.** The equation of the model
with data $(M,K,J)$ is

$$M\,q''(t)+K\,q(t)=J(t)\qquad(t\in I_{0}).$$

A **motion** of the model is a curve $q:J\to\mathbb R^{n}$ of class $C^{2}$
([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]) on an interval
$J\subseteq I_{0}$ with nonempty interior ([[def-interval]]) satisfying the
equation for every $t\in J$. A **datum** at $t_{0}\in I_{0}$ is a pair
$(q_{0},v_{0})\in\mathbb R^{n}\times\mathbb R^{n}$. The **phase system** of
the model is the first-order linear system $z'=A z+b(t)$ on
$I_{0}\times\mathbb R^{2n}$ with $z=(q,v)$ and

$$A=\begin{pmatrix}0&I_{n}\\-M^{-1}K&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad b(t)=\begin{pmatrix}0\\M^{-1}J(t)\end{pmatrix},$$

where $M^{-1}$ is the inverse of $M$. By the product rule and invertibility of
$M$, a $C^{1}$ curve $t\mapsto(q(t),v(t))$ solves the phase system if and only
if $q$ is a motion of the model and $v=q'$. The model is **free** when
$J\equiv0$ and **forced, with generalized force $J$,** otherwise; the read of
$J$ as a prescribed external generalized force is the modelling status of
[[post-cm02-force-superposition]] and
[[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]] for the external contributions
of a force model.

**(c) Quadratic energies and the mass metric.** The **kinetic energy**, the
**potential energy of the stiffness** and the **mechanical energy** of the
model are

$$T(v):=\tfrac12\,v^{\mathsf T}Mv,\qquad U_{K}(q):=\tfrac12\,q^{\mathsf T}Kq,\qquad E(q,v):=T(v)+U_{K}(q),$$

all of energy dimension. $U_{K}$ is defined for every symmetric $K$; the name
records that $K$ is the matrix through which the model enters, and when $K$ is
indefinite $U_{K}$ is not non-negative, the model is not presented by a
potential with a local minimum at the origin, and no stability vocabulary is
attached to it by this item. The quadratic form $v\mapsto v^{\mathsf T}Mv$ is
positive definite and is called the **mass metric** of the model; the word
"metric" records only this positive-definiteness, and no distance on
configuration space is defined here.

**(d) Small-oscillation model at an equilibrium.** Let a mechanical system in
a chart be given by a $C^{2}$ field $q\mapsto G_{\mathrm{kin}}(q)$ of
symmetric positive definite matrices on an open set $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb
R^{n}$ and a $C^{2}$ potential $U:\Omega\to\mathbb R$
([[def-cm-mechanical-vector-field-and-energy-in-a-chart]]), and let
$q_{0}\in\Omega$ be a **mechanical equilibrium**, $\nabla U(q_{0})=0$. Its
**small-oscillation model at $q_{0}$** is the coupled quadratic model with
degrees of freedom $n$, mass metric matrix $M:=G_{\mathrm{kin}}(q_{0})$,
**stiffness matrix** $K_{0}:=D^{2}U(q_{0})$ — the Hessian of the potential
([[def-hessian-and-euclidean-critical-point]], symmetric by
[[cor-hessian-is-symmetric]]) — and zero generalized force, read in the
displacement coordinates $\xi:=q-q_{0}$. When the chart arises from the
generalized-coordinate dictionary of
[[def-cm07-generalized-coordinates-and-forces]], the matrix
$G_{\mathrm{kin}}(q_{0})=DX(q_{0})^{\mathsf T}\mathsf M\,DX(q_{0})$ is the
value at $q_{0}$ of that dictionary's kinetic metric. This clause assigns
model data to the equilibrium; the identification of the assigned model with
the derivative of the mechanical field, and every statement about its motions,
are separate results and are not asserted here.

**(e) Modal vocabulary of the decoupling data.** By
[[thm-cm-quadratic-mode-decomposition]] applied to the symmetric positive
definite $M$ and the symmetric matrix $K$ there are a symmetric positive
definite square root $M^{1/2}$, its inverse $M^{-1/2}$, an orthogonal matrix
$O$ with $O^{\mathsf T}=O^{-1}$, and a diagonal matrix
$\Lambda=\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_{1},\dots,\lambda_{n})$ with
$M^{-1/2}KM^{-1/2}=O\Lambda O^{\mathsf T}$. The **modal coordinates** of the
model are $z:=O^{\mathsf T}M^{1/2}q$, a linear bijection of $\mathbb R^{n}$,
and the **modal vectors** are the columns $u_{i}:=M^{-1/2}Oe_{i}$; the numbers
$\lambda_{1},\dots,\lambda_{n}$ are the **modal stiffnesses**. The identities
$Ku_{i}=\lambda_{i}Mu_{i}$ and $u_{i}^{\mathsf T}Mu_{j}=\delta_{ij}$ are part
of the modal theorem and are used by name on this page. An index $i$ (or the
mode it labels) is **oscillatory** when $\lambda_{i}>0$, with **mode
frequency** $\omega_{i}:=\sqrt{\lambda_{i}}>0$ (the nonnegative square root;
dimension $\tau^{-1}$, read in radians per second under the angle convention
of [[def-cm01-units]]); it is a **zero mode** when $\lambda_{i}=0$; and it is
an **unstable (exponential) direction** when $\lambda_{i}<0$. Two distinct
indices $i\ne j$ are **degenerate** when $\lambda_{i}=\lambda_{j}$; for a real
number $\lambda$ the set $E_{\lambda}:=\{u\in\mathbb R^{n}:(K-\lambda M)u=0\}$
is the **modal eigenspace** of $\lambda$, a linear subspace whose dimension is
the number of indices with $\lambda_{i}=\lambda$. The model is **oscillatory**
when $K$ is non-negative, $q^{\mathsf T}Kq\ge0$ for all $q$; then every modal
stiffness is $\ge0$, the zero modes are the indices with $\lambda_{i}=0$, and
the eigenvalue $0$ has multiplicity $\dim\ker K$.

**(f) Status.** This item introduces objects, vocabulary, domains, regularity
and dimensions for the restricted model class of this page and assigns its
small-oscillation model to a mechanical equilibrium. It contains no
existence, uniqueness, conservation, stability, resonance, degeneracy or
approximation assertion; those are proved on this page as separate items. It
adopts no force law of nature and records no measured value. Every later
statement of this page names the data $(M,K,J)$ or the mechanical data
$(G_{\mathrm{kin}},U,q_{0})$ it uses, and the one-dimensional instance is
recorded in the remarks.
items.strategy: Define the quadratic model class: mass metric, stiffness, prescribed generalized force, quadratic energies, the phase system, the modal vocabulary of the decoupling transform and the small-oscillation model assigned to a mechanical equilibrium; assert nothing beyond the definitions and the recorded dimension bookkeeping.
items.physical_scope: The restricted model class used on this page: a constant mass metric matrix M (symmetric positive definite) and a constant symmetric stiffness matrix K in a chart of n coordinate directions, with an optional prescribed generalized force J(t), and the model equation M q'' + K q = J(t); together with the quadratic kinetic and potential energies, the phase system, the modal vocabulary of the decoupling transform, and the small-oscillation model assigned to a mechanical equilibrium q_0 of a chart mechanical system, whose mass metric is M(q_0) and whose stiffness is the potential Hessian D^2 U(q_0). The item declares vocabulary, domains, regularity and dimensions only; it asserts no existence, uniqueness, conservation, stability, resonance or approximation statement, adopts no force law of nature, records no measured value, and states no empirical applicability. In particular the mass metric and the stiffness are model parameters of the declared chart, not measured quantities, and the quadratic model is an idealization whose accuracy near an equilibrium is quantified only by the approximation theorems of this page.

items.title: The free coupled quadratic model: global existence, the complete modal classification, mode energies, intrinsic degenerate mode subspaces, boundedness and the unstable direction
items.statement:
Global-time, growth and boundedness claims below refer to the unique maximal extension of the autonomous free equation on $\mathbb R$; local motions remain its restrictions. Values at $0$ in coefficient formulas are evaluated on that extension when the original interval omits $0$.

Adopt the free coupled quadratic model of
[[def-cm09-coupled-quadratic-model]] with data $(M,K,J)$ in which
$J\equiv0$, $M$ is symmetric positive definite and $K$ is symmetric, with
modal data $M^{1/2}$, $M^{-1/2}$, $O$, $\Lambda=\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_{1},\dots,\lambda_{n})$,
modal coordinates $z=O^{\mathsf T}M^{1/2}q$ and mode frequencies
$\omega_{i}=\sqrt{\lambda_{i}}$ for $\lambda_{i}>0$. Write
$\kappa_{i}:=\sqrt{-\lambda_{i}}$ for $\lambda_{i}<0$. Then:

1. **Existence and uniqueness on the whole line.** For every $t_{0}\in\mathbb R$
and every datum $(q_{0},v_{0})\in\mathbb R^{2n}$ there is exactly one motion
$q:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^{n}$ with $q(t_{0})=q_{0}$ and $q'(t_{0})=v_{0}$; it
is the unique maximal motion through that datum.
2. **Complete modal classification.** A curve $q:J\to\mathbb R^{n}$ of class
$C^{2}$ on an interval $J\subseteq\mathbb R$ with nonempty interior is a
motion of the free model if and only if its modal coordinates satisfy

$$z_{i}(t)=a_{i}\cos(\omega_{i}t)+b_{i}\sin(\omega_{i}t)\ (\lambda_{i}>0),\qquad z_{i}(t)=a_{i}+b_{i}t\ (\lambda_{i}=0),\qquad z_{i}(t)=a_{i}\cosh(\kappa_{i}t)+b_{i}\sinh(\kappa_{i}t)\ (\lambda_{i}<0)$$

for real numbers $a_{i},b_{i}$; the coefficients are unique and are
determined by the datum of the unique maximal extension through $a_{i}=z_{i}(0)$, $b_{i}=z_{i}'(0)/\omega_{i}$
for $\lambda_{i}>0$, $b_{i}=z_{i}'(0)$ for $\lambda_{i}=0$ and
$b_{i}=z_{i}'(0)/\kappa_{i}$ for $\lambda_{i}<0$.
3. **Energy and mode energies.** Along every motion the mechanical energy is
constant, and with $E_{i}:=\tfrac12\bigl(z_{i}'^{2}+\lambda_{i}z_{i}^{2}\bigr)$
one has $E(q,q')=\sum_{i=1}^{n}E_{i}$ and every $E_{i}$ is constant; for the
families of clause 2,

$$E_{i}=\tfrac12\omega_{i}^{2}\bigl(a_{i}^{2}+b_{i}^{2}\bigr)\ (\lambda_{i}>0),\qquad E_{i}=\tfrac12b_{i}^{2}\ (\lambda_{i}=0),\qquad E_{i}=\tfrac12\kappa_{i}^{2}\bigl(b_{i}^{2}-a_{i}^{2}\bigr)\ (\lambda_{i}<0).$$

4. **Degenerate families are intrinsic.** Let $\lambda$ be a modal stiffness,
let $E_{\lambda}^{S}:=\{u\in\mathbb R^{n}:M^{-1/2}KM^{-1/2}u=\lambda u\}$ and
let $N_{\lambda}:=M^{-1/2}E_{\lambda}^{S}$, a subspace of dimension equal to
the multiplicity of $\lambda$. A motion $q$ satisfies $z_{i}\equiv0$ for every
index $i$ with $\lambda_{i}\ne\lambda$ if and only if $q$ is a $C^{2}$ curve
with $q(t)\in N_{\lambda}$ for all $t$ in its interval and $q''+\lambda q=0$.
Consequently the family of such **pure-$\lambda$ motions** is independent of
the choice of diagonalization $O$: for $\lambda>0$ it consists exactly of
$q(t)=\cos(\omega t)q_{0}+\omega^{-1}\sin(\omega t)q_{1}$ with
$q_{0},q_{1}\in N_{\lambda}$ and $\omega=\sqrt{\lambda}$, for $\lambda=0$ of
$q(t)=q_{0}+tq_{1}$ with $q_{0},q_{1}\in N_{\lambda}$, and for $\lambda<0$ of
$q(t)=\cosh(\kappa t)q_{0}+\kappa^{-1}\sinh(\kappa t)q_{1}$ with
$\kappa=\sqrt{-\lambda}$. These formulas on a local interval are restrictions of their unique maximal extensions; $q_0,q_1$ are the position and velocity of that extension at time $0$, even if the local interval omits $0$. The individual modal vectors $u_{i}$ are not
intrinsic when the multiplicity exceeds one.
5. **Boundedness.** If $K$ is positive definite then every motion is bounded
on $\mathbb R$. If $K$ is non-negative and some $\lambda_{i}=0$, then a
motion with $z_{i}'\equiv b_{i}\ne0$ on a zero mode is unbounded on
$[0,\infty)$: the zero mode is affine, not oscillatory.
6. **Unstable direction.** If $K$ is not non-negative, then $(0,0)$ is not a
Lyapunov stable rest point of the free model
([[def-cm-equilibrium-and-lyapunov-stability]]): there is $\varepsilon_{0}>0$
such that for every $\delta>0$ there are data with
$\lVert(q_{0},v_{0})\rVert_{2}<\delta$ whose motion reaches
$\lVert(q(t),q'(t))\rVert_{2}=\varepsilon_{0}$ at some time $t>0$.

The statement is read for the declared model data; no value of any parameter,
no physical realization and no measured frequency is asserted.
items.strategy: Cases: transport the free system through the modal bijection, solve the three scalar families, read the energy decomposition and boundedness, characterize degenerate pure-lambda families intrinsically, and exhibit the exponential escaping family of a negative modal stiffness.
items.physical_scope: The free coupled quadratic model M q'' + K q = 0 of [[def-cm09-coupled-quadratic-model]] with symmetric positive definite mass metric M and symmetric stiffness K: existence and uniqueness of motions for every datum on the whole real line, the complete classification of motions into oscillatory, affine and exponential modal families with mode frequencies sqrt(lambda_i), the conservation of the mechanical energy with the modal energy decomposition, the intrinsic (basis-free) description of degenerate pure-lambda families in the subspace ker(K - lambda M), boundedness of every motion when K is positive definite, unbounded growth of the affine zero-mode motions and of the exponential directions, and the Lyapunov instability of the rest point of the free model when K has a negative modal stiffness. The result is a conditional statement about the declared model class; it contains no claim that any physical system is described by it, no measured stiffness, mass or frequency, and no empirical qualification beyond the exact idealization of the model.

items.title: Small oscillations at a strict minimum: the linearized model, its normal modes and the Lyapunov stability of the nonlinear equilibrium
items.statement:
Adopt the mechanical system in a chart of
[[def-cm-mechanical-vector-field-and-energy-in-a-chart]] with kinetic metric
field $M:\Omega\to M_{n}(\mathbb R)$ of class $C^{2}$, symmetric positive
definite at every point of the open set $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^{n}$, and
potential $U:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ of class $C^{2}$; write $G$ for its
mechanical vector field on $\Omega\times\mathbb R^{n}$. Let $q_{0}\in\Omega$
be a **strict local minimum** of $U$: $\nabla U(q_{0})=0$ and there is
$r_{0}>0$ with $\overline B(q_{0},r_{0})\subseteq\Omega$ and
$U(q)>U(q_{0})$ for $0<\lVert q-q_{0}\rVert_{2}<r_{0}$. Let
$M_{0}:=M(q_{0})$ and $K:=D^{2}U(q_{0})$. Then:

1. $K$ is symmetric and non-negative, and the small-oscillation model at
$q_{0}$ of clause (d) of [[def-cm09-coupled-quadratic-model]] — the coupled
quadratic model with mass metric matrix $M_{0}$, stiffness $K$ and zero
generalized force, in the displacement coordinates $\xi=q-q_{0}$ — is an
oscillatory model in the sense of clause (e) of that definition;
2. the linearization of $G$ at $(q_{0},0)$ is
$$DG(q_{0},0)(\delta q,\delta v)=\bigl(\delta v,\,-M_{0}^{-1}K\,\delta q\bigr)\qquad(\delta q,\delta v\in\mathbb R^{n}),$$
and for a curve $\xi:J\to\mathbb R^{n}$ of class $C^{2}$ on an interval $J$
with nonempty interior the following are equivalent: $\xi$ is a motion of the
small-oscillation model, $M_{0}\xi''+K\xi=0$ on $J$, and $t\mapsto(\xi(t),\xi'(t))$
solves the linear system $y'=DG(q_{0},0)y$ on $J$;
3. the motions of the small-oscillation model are exactly the modal
superpositions of clause 2 of [[pthm-cm09-free-modes-and-degeneracy]] with
every modal stiffness $\lambda_{i}\ge0$: there are no exponential
pure-$\lambda$ families, every oscillatory frequency is
$\omega_{i}=\sqrt{\lambda_{i}}$, and the pure-$\lambda$ motions of a
degenerate stiffness are the solutions of $q''+\lambda q=0$ with values in
the intrinsic subspace $N_{\lambda}=M_{0}^{-1/2}\{u:M_{0}^{-1/2}KM_{0}^{-1/2}u=\lambda u\}$;
4. $(q_{0},0)$ is a Lyapunov stable equilibrium of the nonlinear mechanical
system: for every $\varepsilon>0$ with
$\overline B((q_{0},0),\varepsilon)\subseteq\Omega\times\mathbb R^{n}$ there
is $\delta>0$ such that every maximal solution of $z'=G(z)$ with
$\lVert z(0)-(q_{0},0)\rVert_{2}<\delta$ exists for all $t\ge0$ and stays
within distance $\varepsilon$ of $(q_{0},0)$.

No asymptotic attraction, no all-time validity of the linear model as an
approximation of the nonlinear motion, and no measured frequency is asserted.
items.strategy: Direct: assemble the assigned small-oscillation model from the definition, identify the derivative linearization with the model phase system, read the non-negative normal-mode classification, and invoke the energy-stability theorem for the nonlinear statement.
items.physical_scope: A mechanical system in a chart at a strict local minimum of its potential: the assigned small-oscillation quadratic model with mass metric M(q_0) and stiffness the Hessian D^2 U(q_0) (symmetric and non-negative), the identification of that model with the derivative linearization of the mechanical field, the complete normal-mode classification of the linearized motions with frequencies sqrt(lambda_i) and no exponential directions, and the Lyapunov stability of the nonlinear equilibrium by exact energy conservation. The stability conclusion is a statement about the declared chart model; it asserts no asymptotic attraction, no measured frequency, no particular physical system and no empirical claim, and the accuracy of the linear model as an approximation of the nonlinear motion is a separate finite-time statement on this page.

items.title: Finite-time error control for the small-oscillation approximation: the quadratic remainder of the mechanical field and the variation-of-constants bound
items.statement:
Let $n\ge1$, let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^{n}$ be open, let
$M:\Omega\to M_{n}(\mathbb R)$ be a field of class $C^{3}$ with $M(q)$
symmetric positive definite for every $q\in\Omega$, and let
$U:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ be of class $C^{3}$ with $\nabla U(q_{0})=0$ at a point
$q_{0}\in\Omega$. Let $G$ be the mechanical vector field of
[[def-cm-mechanical-vector-field-and-energy-in-a-chart]] on
$\Omega\times\mathbb R^{n}$, let $r_{0}>0$ satisfy
$\overline B(q_{0},r_{0})\subseteq\Omega$ and define
$F:\{\zeta=(\delta q,\delta v):q_{0}+\delta q\in\Omega\}\to\mathbb R^{2n}$ by
$F(\delta q,\delta v):=G(q_{0}+\delta q,\delta v)$. Put
$A:=DF(0)=DG(q_{0},0)$. Then:

1. $F$ is of class $C^{2}$, $F(0)=0$, $F$ is locally Lipschitz in the state
variable, and
$$DG(q_{0},0)(\delta q,\delta v)=\bigl(\delta v,\,-M(q_{0})^{-1}D^{2}U(q_{0})\,\delta q\bigr);$$
moreover there are constants $C,L\ge0$ with
$$\lVert F(\zeta)-A\zeta\rVert_{2}\le C\lVert\zeta\rVert_{2}^{2},\qquad \lVert F(\zeta)\rVert_{2}\le L\lVert\zeta\rVert_{2}\qquad(\lVert\zeta\rVert_{2}\le r_{0});$$
one may take $L=\sup_{\lVert\eta\rVert_{2}\le r_{0}}\lVert DF(\eta)\rVert$
([[def-operator-norm]]) and $C=\Lambda/2$ for any Lipschitz constant
$\Lambda$ of $DF$ on the closed ball
$\overline B(0,r_{0})\subseteq\mathbb R^{2n}$ ([[def-metric-ball]]).
2. For every datum $z_{0}=(q_{0}+\delta q_{0},v_{0})$ with
$\delta:=\lVert(\delta q_{0},v_{0})\rVert_{2}>0$ and every $T>0$ with
$\delta e^{LT}<r_{0}$, the maximal solution $z=(q,v)$ of $z'=G(z)$ with
$z(0)=z_{0}$ is defined on $[0,T]$ ([[def-maximal-ode-solution]]) and
satisfies, for every $t\in[0,T]$,
$$\lVert z(t)-y(t)\rVert_{2}\le C\delta^{2}\,t\,e^{(\lVert A\rVert+2L)t},$$
where $y(t)=(q_0+\xi(t),\eta(t))$ and $\widetilde y=(\xi,\eta):\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^{2n}$ solves $\widetilde y'=A\widetilde y$, $\widetilde y(0)=(\delta q_0,v_0)$. Thus $y$ is the linear approximation translated back to the original chart.
3. Writing $\widetilde y=(\xi,\eta)$ for the displacement linear solution of clause 2, the first
component $\xi$ is exactly the unique motion of the small-oscillation model
at $q_{0}$ of clause (d) of [[def-cm09-coupled-quadratic-model]] with datum
$(\delta q_{0},v_{0})$: $\xi$ is $C^{2}$ on $\mathbb R$ with
$M(q_{0})\xi''+D^{2}U(q_{0})\xi=0$, $\xi(0)=\delta q_{0}$ and
$\xi'(0)=v_{0}$.

No all-time statement, no statement for data violating the smallness
condition $\delta e^{LT}<r_{0}$, and no value of any measured quantity is
asserted.
items.strategy: Direct: prove the quadratic-remainder bounds for the translated mechanical field by compactness and the fundamental theorem along rays, then apply the finite-time linearization theorem and identify the linear solution with the small-oscillation motion.
items.physical_scope: Finite-time error control for the small-oscillation model of a mechanical system in a chart at a mechanical equilibrium: for a C^3 kinetic metric field and a C^3 potential with vanishing gradient at q_0, the mechanical field is C^2 near the equilibrium, its Taylor remainder at the linearization is quadratic with constants obtained from compactness, and the finite-time variation-of-constants estimate bounds the difference between the nonlinear motion and the linearized (normal-mode) motion by C delta^2 t exp((||A||+2L)t) on every horizon T with delta exp(LT)<r_0. The statement is a conditional finite-time estimate for the declared chart model under explicit regularity and smallness hypotheses; it asserts no all-time validity of the linear approximation, no stability conclusion, no large-data statement and no empirical claim, and the constants depend on the model data only through its behaviour on the stated ball.

items.title: The forced coupled quadratic model: decoupled modal responses, sinusoidal drive, resonance at the modal frequencies and boundedness away from resonance
items.statement:
Adopt the coupled quadratic model of [[def-cm09-coupled-quadratic-model]] with
data $(M,K,J)$ in which $M$ is symmetric positive definite, $K$ is symmetric
and non-negative, $I_{0}\subseteq\mathbb R$ is an interval with nonempty
interior and $J:I_{0}\to\mathbb R^{n}$ is continuous; let
$O,\Lambda=\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_{1},\dots,\lambda_{n})$,
$\omega_{i}=\sqrt{\lambda_{i}}$ for $\lambda_{i}>0$ and the modal coordinates
$z=O^{\mathsf T}M^{1/2}q$ be the modal data of clause (e) of that definition,
and call $\psi:=O^{\mathsf T}M^{-1/2}J$ the **modal force**. Fix
$t_{0}\in I_{0}$ and a datum $(q_{0},v_{0})$, and write
$\xi_{i}:=z_{i}(t_{0})$, $\eta_{i}:=z_{i}'(t_{0})$ for the modal data of the
motion. Then:

1. **Unique motion and modal convolution.** There is exactly one motion
$q:I_{0}\to\mathbb R^{n}$ with that datum; it is $q=M^{-1/2}Oz$ with

$$z_{i}(t)=\xi_{i}\cos\bigl(\omega_{i}(t-t_{0})\bigr)+\frac{\eta_{i}}{\omega_{i}}\sin\bigl(\omega_{i}(t-t_{0})\bigr)+\frac{1}{\omega_{i}}\int_{t_{0}}^{t}\sin\bigl(\omega_{i}(t-s)\bigr)\psi_{i}(s)\,ds\quad(\lambda_{i}>0),$$

$$z_{i}(t)=\xi_{i}+\eta_{i}(t-t_{0})+\int_{t_{0}}^{t}(t-s)\psi_{i}(s)\,ds\quad(\lambda_{i}=0).$$

2. **Sinusoidal generalized force.** Suppose $I_{0}=\mathbb R$ and
$J(t)=J_{0}\cos(\Omega t)$ with $J_{0}\in\mathbb R^{n}$ and $\Omega\ge0$, so
that $\psi(t)=\psi_{0}\cos(\Omega t)$ with
$\psi_{0}=O^{\mathsf T}M^{-1/2}J_{0}$. Then for each index $i$:
   (a) if $\lambda_{i}>0$ and $\Omega^{2}\ne\lambda_{i}$, then
   $z_{i}^{\mathrm{p}}(t):=\psi_{0,i}\cos(\Omega t)/(\lambda_{i}-\Omega^{2})$
   solves $z_{i}''+\lambda_{i}z_{i}=\psi_{0,i}\cos(\Omega t)$ on $\mathbb R$,
   with amplitude $|\psi_{0,i}|/|\lambda_{i}-\Omega^{2}|$;
   (b) if $\lambda_{i}>0$ and $\Omega^{2}=\lambda_{i}$, then
   $z_{i}^{\mathrm{p}}(t):=\psi_{0,i}\,t\sin(\omega_{i}t)/(2\omega_{i})$
   solves that equation and is unbounded on $[0,\infty)$ when
   $\psi_{0,i}\ne0$;
   (c) if $\lambda_{i}=0$ and $\Omega>0$, then
   $z_{i}^{\mathrm{p}}(t):=-\psi_{0,i}\cos(\Omega t)/\Omega^{2}$ solves
   $z_{i}''=\psi_{0,i}\cos(\Omega t)$ and is bounded; if $\lambda_{i}=0$ and
   $\Omega=0$, then $z_{i}^{\mathrm{p}}(t):=\psi_{0,i}t^{2}/2$ solves
   $z_{i}''=\psi_{0,i}$ and is unbounded on $[0,\infty)$ when
   $\psi_{0,i}\ne0$.
3. **Reduction, resonance and boundedness.** In every case of clause 2 the
modal particular functions $z_{i}^{\mathrm{p}}$ combine into the particular
motion $q^{\mathrm{p}}:=M^{-1/2}Oz^{\mathrm{p}}$ of the model, and every
motion of the model on $\mathbb R$ is $q=q^{\mathrm{p}}+q^{\mathrm{h}}$ with
$q^{\mathrm{h}}$ a motion of the free model of
[[def-cm09-coupled-quadratic-model]]. Consequently:
   (a) **resonance.** If some index $i$ has $\psi_{0,i}\ne0$ and either
   $\lambda_{i}>0$ with $\Omega^{2}=\lambda_{i}$, or $\lambda_{i}=0$ with
   $\Omega=0$, then every motion of the model is unbounded on $[0,\infty)$;
   (b) **boundedness.** If $K$ is positive definite and no index $i$ with
   $\psi_{0,i}\ne0$ satisfies $\Omega^{2}=\lambda_{i}$, then every motion of
   the model is bounded on $[0,\infty)$.
   The resonant drive angular frequencies are exactly the values
   $\Omega=\sqrt{\lambda_{i}}$ with $\lambda_{i}>0$ and $\psi_{0,i}\ne0$,
   together with $\Omega=0$ when some index with $\lambda_{i}=0$ has
   $\psi_{0,i}\ne0$.

The generalized force is prescribed external data in the modelling status of
[[post-cm04-sinusoidal-drive-model]]: it is a function of time alone, the
source is not modelled dynamically, and no back-reaction, damping, measured
response or empirical value is asserted.

items.title: Averaging for a weakly damped oscillator: the rotating-frame amplitude, the averaged exponential energy decay and the order-$\varepsilon$ bound on the $O(1/\varepsilon)$ time scale
items.statement:
Adopt the strictly damped oscillator model of
[[post-cm04-linear-damping-model]] with fixed data $m>0$, $k>0$ and drag
coefficient $c=\varepsilon\gamma$, where $\varepsilon>0$ and $\gamma>0$ are
given; its equation is

$$m\,x''(t)+\varepsilon\gamma\,x'(t)+k\,x(t)=0 .$$

Put $\omega_{0}:=\sqrt{k/m}$ and identify $\mathbb C$ with $\mathbb R^{2}$.
For a motion $x$ define the **rotating-frame amplitude**

$$\zeta(t):=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\omega_{0}}}\bigl(\omega_{0}x(t)+i\,x'(t)\bigr)e^{i\omega_{0}t}\in\mathbb C,$$

and define $F:\mathbb R\times\mathbb C\to\mathbb C$ by

$$F(t,\zeta):=-\frac{i\gamma}{m}\,e^{i\omega_{0}t}\bigl(\cos(\omega_{0}t)\operatorname{Im}\zeta-\sin(\omega_{0}t)\operatorname{Re}\zeta\bigr).$$

Then:

1. **Global motions and the slow system.** Every datum
$(t_{0},x_{0},v_{0})\in\mathbb R^{3}$ has exactly one maximal motion, and it
is defined on all of $\mathbb R$. The map $x\mapsto\zeta$ is a bijection
from the motions $x:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ of the model onto the solutions
$\zeta:\mathbb R\to\mathbb C$ of the first-order system
$\zeta'=\varepsilon F(t,\zeta)$, with inverse
$\zeta\mapsto x(t)=\sqrt{2/\omega_{0}}\operatorname{Re}\bigl(e^{-i\omega_{0}t}\zeta(t)\bigr)$.
2. **Averaging data.** $F$ is of class $C^{\infty}$ on
$\mathbb R\times\mathbb C$, is $P$-periodic in $t$ with $P:=2\pi/\omega_{0}$,
and its average in the sense of
[[def-cm-averaging-data-and-averaged-field]] is
$\bar F(\zeta)=-\gamma\zeta/(2m)$; the averaged system is
$\zeta'=-\varepsilon\gamma\zeta/(2m)$, with the global solution
$\bar\zeta(t)=\zeta_{0}e^{-\varepsilon\gamma t/(2m)}$ for the datum
$\zeta_{0}=\zeta(0)$.
3. **Order-$\varepsilon$ estimate on the $O(1/\varepsilon)$ time scale.**
Let $\zeta_{0}\in\mathbb C$ with $\lvert\zeta_{0}\rvert>0$, let
$0<\rho<R$ be real numbers and put
$$M:=\frac{\gamma}{m}\sqrt2\,\bigl(\lvert\zeta_{0}\rvert+R\bigr),\qquad L:=\frac{\gamma}{m}\sqrt2,\qquad B:=2MP,\qquad B_{1}:=2LP,$$
$$K:=e^{LA}\bigl[B+(LB+B_{1}M)A\bigr]$$
for a parameter $A>0$. Suppose $\varepsilon K<\rho$ and suppose the averaged
solution satisfies $\lVert\bar\zeta(t)-\zeta_{0}\rVert_{2}\le R-\rho$ for
every $t\in[0,A/\varepsilon]$; this holds whenever
$\lvert\zeta_{0}\rvert>R-\rho$ and
$\gamma A/(2m)\le\ln\bigl(\lvert\zeta_{0}\rvert/(\lvert\zeta_{0}\rvert-(R-\rho))\bigr)$.
Then the solution $\zeta$ of $\zeta'=\varepsilon F(t,\zeta)$ with
$\zeta(0)=\zeta_{0}$ exists on $[0,A/\varepsilon]$ and satisfies
$$\lVert\zeta(t)-\bar\zeta(t)\rVert_{2}\le\varepsilon K\qquad(0\le t\le A/\varepsilon).$$
4. **Energy reading.** For every motion the mechanical energy satisfies
$$E(t):=\tfrac12m\,x'(t)^{2}+\tfrac12k\,x(t)^{2}=m\omega_{0}\lvert\zeta(t)\rvert^{2},$$
so with $E_{0}:=E(0)=m\omega_{0}\lvert\zeta_{0}\rvert^{2}$ the estimate of
clause 3 gives
$$\bigl\lvert E(t)-E_{0}e^{-\varepsilon\gamma t/m}\bigr\rvert\le m\omega_{0}\,\varepsilon K\bigl(2\lvert\zeta_{0}\rvert+\varepsilon K\bigr)\qquad(0\le t\le A/\varepsilon).$$

The averaged system is a different model from the exact one, and the
statements are conditional on the displayed smallness and trapping
hypotheses; no exact decay law, no measured decay rate, and no empirical
claim is asserted.

items.title: Scope of the coupled quadratic model: zero modes, degenerate eigenspaces, unstable quadratic directions and the limits of the approximation statements
items.statement:
A **zero mode** of a coupled quadratic model is an index with modal
stiffness $\lambda_{i}=0$ ([[def-cm09-coupled-quadratic-model]] clause (e));
the multiplicity of the value $0$ is $\dim\ker K$, and it counts the
independent directions in which the quadratic model exerts no restoring
force. By clause 2 of [[pthm-cm09-free-modes-and-degeneracy]] the free motion
in such a direction is affine, $z_{i}(t)=a_{i}+b_{i}t$, not oscillatory; for
$b_{i}\ne0$ it is unbounded on $[0,\infty)$. The classical instance is the
translation mode of a chain or molecule: the linearisation of a
translation-invariant model at a non-isolated minimum has a flat
second-order direction, and the "mode" of zero frequency is the uniform
motion of the whole system rather than a vibration. A constant generalized
force component along a zero mode produces quadratic growth in time by
clause 2(c) of [[pthm-cm09-forced-modal-response]], the degenerate analogue
of resonance; the model has no bounded steady response in that direction.
Zero modes are therefore excluded whenever a statement about oscillations
alone is intended: at a strict local minimum the stiffness is positive
semidefinite with $\ker K$ possibly nontrivial only if the minimum is not
isolated along those directions, and the Lyapunov stability of
[[pthm-cm09-linearization-at-a-strict-minimum]] remains valid in that case
because it does not use positivity of the stiffness.

## Degenerate modal stiffnesses

If a modal stiffness $\lambda$ has multiplicity $m>1$, the individual
eigenvectors and hence the individual modal vectors $u_{i}$ of a chosen
diagonalisation are **not** intrinsic: every orthonormal basis of the
eigenspace gives an equally valid decoupling. What is intrinsic is the
subspace $N_{\lambda}$ and its pure-$\lambda$ family of motions, exactly as
clause 4 of [[pthm-cm09-free-modes-and-degeneracy]] records: the pure-$\lambda$
motions are the solutions of $q''+\lambda q=0$ with values in
$N_{\lambda}$, a family with $2m$ parameters, and for $\lambda>0$ all of them
oscillate with the single frequency $\omega=\sqrt{\lambda}$. A statement
about "the $i$-th mode" must therefore be read as a statement about a chosen
basis vector, while the frequency, the subspace and the multi-parameter
family are the basis-independent objects. Resonance of a degenerate family
with a prescribed sinusoidal force is likewise basis-independent: it occurs
exactly when the modal force vanishes in no direction of $N_{\lambda}$
(clause 2 and the remarks of [[pthm-cm09-forced-modal-response]]).

## Unstable quadratic directions

An **unstable (exponential) direction** is an index with $\lambda_{i}<0$
([[def-cm09-coupled-quadratic-model]] clause (e)). Its free motion is the
hyperbolic family $a\cosh(\kappa t)+b\sinh(\kappa t)$ with
$\kappa=\sqrt{-\lambda_{i}}$, which grows exponentially whenever it is not
identically zero, and clause 6 of [[pthm-cm09-free-modes-and-degeneracy]]
proves accordingly that the rest point of the free quadratic model is not
Lyapunov stable ([[def-cm-equilibrium-and-lyapunov-stability]]). For a
mechanical system in a chart at a **critical** point $q_{0}$ of the potential
that is not a minimum — for instance a symmetric saddle or a strict maximum —
the stiffness $K=D^{2}U(q_{0})$ may have negative eigenvalues
([[def-hessian-and-euclidean-critical-point]]), and the corresponding
exponential directions of the linearised model exhibit the local saddle
behaviour. The linear calculation by itself certifies nothing about the
nonlinear system: the nonlinear instability of $(q_{0},0)$ follows from
[[thm-cm-instability-of-a-hyperbolic-saddle]] only when the derivative
$DG(q_{0},0)$ of the mechanical field
([[def-cm-mechanical-vector-field-and-energy-in-a-chart]]) is **hyperbolic**
— no eigenvalue on the imaginary axis, in particular no zero mode — and has
an eigenvalue with positive real part. When a zero mode is present the
linearisation is not hyperbolic and the exponential-mode argument does not
apply; a higher-order analysis is then required and is not supplied here.
Conversely, a negative eigenvalue of the stiffness is necessary but not
sufficient for a physical instability statement, because the nonlinear terms
may dominate in ways the quadratic model does not see.

## Limits of the approximation statements

Three separate qualifications belong to the results of this page.

- **The quadratic model is exact only for quadratic data.** The model
$Mq''+Kq=J$ is a declared model class; it coincides with a mechanical chart
system $G_{\mathrm{kin}}(q)q''+\cdots=-\nabla U(q)$ only when the kinetic
metric is constant and the potential is quadratic. The small-oscillation
model at an equilibrium is a first-order Taylor model, and
[[pthm-cm09-linearization-at-a-strict-minimum]] identifies it with the
derivative linearization without asserting that it approximates the
nonlinear motion.

- **The linearization error bound is finite-time and small-data.** The
estimate of [[pthm-cm09-linearization-error-bound]],
$\lVert z(t)-y(t)\rVert_{2}\le C\delta^{2}te^{(\lVert A\rVert+2L)t}$ on
$[0,T]$ under $\delta e^{LT}<r_{0}$, controls the discrepancy of the
nonlinear and linear motions only for the stated horizon, datum size and
regularity; the exponential factor grows with $T$, and no all-time
closeness, stability or instability conclusion follows from it.

- **The averaging estimate is a comparison, not an identity.** The
order-$\varepsilon$ bound of [[pthm-cm09-averaging-for-weak-damping]] holds
on the $O(1/\varepsilon)$ horizon under the displayed smallness, trapping and
constant hypotheses, and compares the exact weakly damped model with a
different, averaged model; it is not an exact decay law of the damped
oscillator, and its constants $M,L,K$ depend on the chosen ball and horizon.

Beyond the mathematical qualifications, the parameters of the models of this
page — masses, stiffnesses, damping coefficients, drive amplitudes and
frequencies — are model data. A value of such a parameter taken from a
calibration experiment is an empirical premise carrying the apparatus
conditions and the measurement uncertainty, and no claim of this page
identifies a model frequency with an observed spectral line without a
specified measurement model, which is not supplied here.

items.title: Two coupled masses on a line: the in-phase and anti-phase normal modes, their frequencies, mode-energies and the zero-stiffness translation mode
items.statement:
Global-time, growth and boundedness claims below refer to the unique maximal extension of the autonomous free equation on $\mathbb R$; local motions remain its restrictions. Values at $0$ in coefficient formulas are evaluated on that extension when the original interval omits $0$.

Consider two particle labels of equal mass $m>0$ constrained to a line, with
coordinates $x_{1},x_{2}$ in metres read in a fixed inertial frame
([[def-cm01-units]]). Each label is attached to a fixed point by a spring of
stiffness $k>0$ and the labels are coupled to each other by a spring of
stiffness $c>0$; both constants are read in kilograms per second squared.
The model is the coupled quadratic model of
[[def-cm09-coupled-quadratic-model]] with $n=2$, coordinates $q=(x_{1},x_{2})$,
mass metric matrix $M=mI_{2}$ and stiffness

$$K=\begin{pmatrix}k+c&-c\\-c&k+c\end{pmatrix},$$

so that the equation $Mq''+Kq=0$ is the linear chain
$m x_{1}''=-(k+c)x_{1}+cx_{2}$, $m x_{2}''=cx_{1}-(k+c)x_{2}$. Then:

1. the vectors $u_{\pm}:=(1,\pm1)/\sqrt{2m}$ satisfy
$u_{+}^{\mathsf T}Mu_{+}=u_{-}^{\mathsf T}Mu_{-}=1$,
$u_{+}^{\mathsf T}Mu_{-}=0$ and $Ku_{\pm}=\lambda_{\pm}Mu_{\pm}$ with
$$\lambda_{+}=\frac{k}{m},\qquad \lambda_{-}=\frac{k+2c}{m};$$
2. the modal coordinates are $z_{\pm}=e_{\pm}^{\mathsf T}M^{1/2}q$ with
$e_{\pm}=(1,\pm1)/\sqrt2$, that is $z_{+}=\sqrt{m/2}\,(x_{1}+x_{2})$ and
$z_{-}=\sqrt{m/2}\,(x_{1}-x_{2})$, and every motion is
$$q(t)=\bigl(A\cos(\omega_{+}t)+B\sin(\omega_{+}t)\bigr)u_{+}+\bigl(C\cos(\omega_{-}t)+D\sin(\omega_{-}t)\bigr)u_{-}$$
with $\omega_{+}=\sqrt{k/m}$ and $\omega_{-}=\sqrt{(k+2c)/m}$;
3. the initial data $q(0)=u_{+}$, $q'(0)=0$ excite exactly the in-phase mode
$q(t)=\cos(\omega_{+}t)u_{+}$, whose mechanical energy is the constant
$E=k/(2m)$; the data $q(0)=u_{-}$, $q'(0)=0$ excite exactly the anti-phase
mode $q(t)=\cos(\omega_{-}t)u_{-}$, with $E=(k+2c)/(2m)$;
4. the in-phase frequency $\omega_{+}$ is independent of the coupling $c$
and the anti-phase frequency $\omega_{-}$ is strictly increasing in $c$;
5. if $k=0$ while $c>0$, then $\lambda_{+}=0$ and $u_{+}$ spans a zero mode:
the general motion is $q(t)=(A+Bt)u_{+}+(C\cos(\omega_{-}t)+D\sin(\omega_{-}t))u_{-}$,
the pair translates freely as a whole and only the relative coordinate
oscillates, at frequency $\sqrt{2c/m}$.
